Without pollinators,
the garden goes dark.

Bees, butterflies, moths, bats and birds carry pollen from flower to flower. That is how many of our fruits, vegetables and wild plants make seeds. We made this site to show you who they are, what they are up against, and how kids can help.

Seeds for our neighborhood

Step 1 · Seed pick-up

We worked with the Williamson County Conservation Foundation (WCCF) to learn which plants and seeds attract pollinators. They also gave us wildflower seed packets free of cost.

Step 2 · Seed distribution

Then we went door to door and handed out the seeds to our neighbors so they can grow flowers for pollinators.

Meeting the experts

🐝 Two Hives Honey

We met the beekeepers at Two Hives Honey, a local honey farm near Austin, to learn about pollinators, especially bees, from people who care for hives every day. First we learned about bees inside, then we suited up and visited the real hives.

About our team and mission

We are the EcoDragons

A FIRST LEGO League team of eight. This season's BioGlow theme is all about nature and wildlife, and we build SPIKE Prime robots to solve nature-inspired LEGO challenges.

Our focus: Pollinators and seeds. Bees, butterflies, moths, bats and birds carry pollen so plants can make seeds and crops can grow, and many animals spread those seeds to new places.

The problem: Many people don't know how much we depend on pollinators, or that they are losing flowers, safe homes and clean air, often because of things people do.

Our solution: This website, where anyone can meet the pollinators, see what threatens them, take a quiz and pick simple ways to help. We also handed out seed packets around our neighborhood to grow more flowers for pollinators.

Our goal: Teach people safer ways to live alongside pollinators, so they can thrive and help our community grow with more crops, flowers and diverse wildlife.

Our team: A strong team of highly motivated 3rd and 4th graders.
